claim: In insects, the SoxB gene Dichaete is the only Sox gene known to be involved in segmentation.
source: In insects, the SoxB gene Dichaete is the only Sox gene known to be involved in segmentation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract without supporting data in the manuscript, but is presented as established knowledge from prior research.

claim: Dichaete does not appear to be involved in spider segmentation.
source: While Dichaete does not appear to be involved in spider segmentation, we found that the closely related Sox21b-1 gene acts as a gap gene during formation of anterior segments and is also part of the segmentation clock for development of the segment addition zone and sequential addition of opisthosomal segments.
evidence: This claim is supported by the expression analysis presented in the manuscript showing Dichaete is not expressed in patterns consistent with segmentation roles.

claim: Sox21b-1 acts as a gap gene during formation of anterior segments in the spider Parasteatoda tepidariorum.
source: While Dichaete does not appear to be involved in spider segmentation, we found that the closely related Sox21b-1 gene acts as a gap gene during formation of anterior segments and is also part of the segmentation clock for development of the segment addition zone and sequential addition of opisthosomal segments.
evidence: This is supported by expression patterns and RNAi knockdown experiments showing loss of leg-bearing segments.

claim: Sox21b-1 is part of the segmentation clock for development of the segment addition zone and sequential addition of opisthosomal segments.
source: While Dichaete does not appear to be involved in spider segmentation, we found that the closely related Sox21b-1 gene acts as a gap gene during formation of anterior segments and is also part of the segmentation clock for development of the segment addition zone and sequential addition of opisthosomal segments.
evidence: This is supported by expression patterns in the SAZ and RNAi knockdown experiments showing loss of opisthosomal segments.

claim: Arthropod diversification and success are at least in part explained by their segmented body plan.
source: Arthropods are the most speciose and widespread of the animal phyla, and it is thought that their diversification and success are at least in part explained by their segmented body plan (Tautz, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Insects utilize either derived long germ embryogenesis or short/intermediate germ embryogenesis.
source: In terms of development, insects utilise either derived long germ embryogenesis, where all body segments are made more or less simultaneously, or short/intermediate germ embryogenesis, where a few anterior segments are specified and posterior segments are added sequentially from a growth or segment addition zone (SAZ) (Peel et al., 2005; Davis and Patel, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: In long germ embryogenesis, all body segments are made more or less simultaneously.
source: In terms of development, insects utilise either derived long germ embryogenesis, where all body segments are made more or less simultaneously, or short/intermediate germ embryogenesis, where a few anterior segments are specified and posterior segments are added sequentially from a growth or segment addition zone (SAZ) (Peel et al., 2005; Davis and Patel, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: In short/intermediate germ embryogenesis, a few anterior segments are specified and posterior segments are added sequentially from a growth or segment addition zone (SAZ).
source: In terms of development, insects utilise either derived long germ embryogenesis, where all body segments are made more or less simultaneously, or short/intermediate germ embryogenesis, where a few anterior segments are specified and posterior segments are added sequentially from a growth or segment addition zone (SAZ) (Peel et al., 2005; Davis and Patel, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Segmentation in the ancestral arthropod resembled the short germ mode seen in most insects.
source: It is thought that segmentation in the ancestral arthropod resembled the short germ mode seen in most insects (Peel et al., 2005; McGregor et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: In the spider prosoma, the cheliceral and pedipalpal segments are generated by dynamic waves of hedgehog (hh) and orthodenticle (otd) expression.
source: In the anterior tagma, the prosoma or cephalothorax, the cheliceral and pedipalpal segments are generated by dynamic waves of hedgehog (hh) and orthodenticle (otd) expression (Kanayama et al., 2011; Pechmann et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The leg-bearing segments in the spider prosoma are specified by gap gene like functions of hunchback (hb) and distal-less (dll).
source: The leg-bearing segments are specified by gap gene like functions of hunchback (hb) and distal-less (dll) (Pechmann et al., 2011; Schwager et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The segments of the spider opisthosoma are generated sequentially from a SAZ.
source: In contrast, the segments of the posterior tagma, the opisthosoma or abdomen, are generated sequentially from a SAZ.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research in the following sentence.

claim: Sequential segment generation in the spider opisthosoma is regulated by dynamic interactions between Delta-Notch and Wnt8 signalling to regulate caudal (cad).
source: This process is regulated by dynamic interactions between Delta-Notch and Wnt8 signalling to regulate caudal (cad), which in turn is required for oscillatory expression of pair-rule gene orthologues including even-skipped (eve), and runt (run) (McGregor et al., 2009; McGregor et al., 2008b; Schönauer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: caudal (cad) is required for oscillatory expression of pair-rule gene orthologues including even-skipped (eve), and runt (run) in the spider opisthosoma.
source: This process is regulated by dynamic interactions between Delta-Notch and Wnt8 signalling to regulate caudal (cad), which in turn is required for oscillatory expression of pair-rule gene orthologues including even-skipped (eve), and runt (run) (McGregor et al., 2009; McGregor et al., 2008b; Schönauer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Pair-rule gene orthologues are not involved in the production of the prosomal segments in spiders.
source: Interestingly, these pair-rule gene orthologues are not involved in the production of the prosomal segments (Schönauer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Dichaete is required for correct embryonic segmentation in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: The Group B Sox (Sry-Related High-Mobility Group box) family gene Dichaete is required for correct embryonic segmentation in the long germ insect D. melanogaster, where it regulates pair-rule gene expression (Nambu and Nambu, 1996; Russell et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Dichaete regulates pair-rule gene expression in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: The Group B Sox (Sry-Related High-Mobility Group box) family gene Dichaete is required for correct embryonic segmentation in the long germ insect D. melanogaster, where it regulates pair-rule gene expression (Nambu and Nambu, 1996; Russell et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: A Dichaete orthologue is likely involved in segmentation in the short germ insect Tribolium castaneum.
source: Interestingly, it was recently discovered that a Dichaete orthologue is also likely involved in segmentation in the short germ insect T. castaneum (Clark and Peel, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Dichaete can play different roles in D. melanogaster and T. castaneum consistent with the generation of segments simultaneously via a gap gene mechanism in the former and sequentially from a posterior SAZ in the latter.
source: However, it appears that despite these similarities, Dichaete can play different roles in D. melanogaster and T. castaneum consistent with the generation of segments simultaneously via a gap gene mechanism in the former and sequentially from a posterior SAZ in the latter (Clark and Peel, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: 14 Sox genes were characterized in the genome of the spider P. tepidariorum.
source: We recently described the characterisation of 14 Sox genes in the genome of the spider P. tepidariorum (Paese et al., 2017)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: Several of the spider Sox genes are represented by multiple copies likely produced during the whole genome duplication (WGD) in the lineage leading to this arachnid.
source: and that several of the spider Sox genes are represented by multiple copies likely produced during the whole genome duplication (WGD) in the lineage leading to this arachnid (Paese et al., 2017; Schwager et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Sox21b-1 is expressed in both the prosoma and opisthosoma before and during segmentation in P. tepidariorum.
source: Interestingly, while Dichaete is not expressed in a pattern consistent with a role in segmentation (Paese et al., 2017), we found that the closely related SoxB gene, Sox21b-1, is expressed in both the prosoma and opisthosoma before and during segmentation (Paese et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: Sox21b-1 has a gap-like gene function and is required for the generation of the four leg-bearing segments in the spider prosoma.
source: In the prosoma, Sox21b-1 has a gap-like gene function and is required for the generation of the four leg-bearing segments.
evidence: This is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments and expression analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Sox21b-1 acts upstream of both Delta-Notch and Wnt8 signalling to regulate the formation of the SAZ.
source: In addition, Sox21b-1 appears to act upstream of both Delta-Notch and Wnt8 signalling to regulate the formation of the SAZ, and knockdown of Sox21b-1 results in truncated embryos missing all opisthosomal segments.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis in Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos showing loss of Delta and Wnt8 expression.

claim: Knockdown of Sox21b-1 results in truncated embryos missing all opisthosomal segments.
source: In addition, Sox21b-1 appears to act upstream of both Delta-Notch and Wnt8 signalling to regulate the formation of the SAZ, and knockdown of Sox21b-1 results in truncated embryos missing all opisthosomal segments.
evidence: This is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments presented in the manuscript.

claim: Sox21b-1 is required for segmentation in both the prosoma and opisthosoma regions of the developing spider embryo.
source: Therefore, while prosomal and opisthosomal segments are generated by different mechanisms in the spider, our analysis shows that Sox21b-1 is required for segmentation in both regions of the developing spider embryo.
evidence: This is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments and expression analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: P. tepidariorum Sox21b-1 and its paralog Sox21b-2 are members of the Sox group B, closely related to the Drosophila Dichaete and Sox21b genes.
source: Our phylogenetic analysis indicates that P. tepidariorum Sox21b-1 and its paralog Sox21b-2 are members of the Sox group B, closely related to the Drosophila Dichaete and Sox21b genes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by phylogenetic analysis presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: In insects, Dichaete, Sox21a and Sox21b are clustered in the genome.
source: In insects (McKimmie et al., 2005; Wilson and Dearden, 2008), Dichaete, Sox21a and Sox21b are clustered in the genome, however, both Sox21b paralogs are dispersed in the spider genome (Paese et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Both Sox21b paralogs are dispersed in the spider genome.
source: In insects (McKimmie et al., 2005; Wilson and Dearden, 2008), Dichaete, Sox21a and Sox21b are clustered in the genome, however, both Sox21b paralogs are dispersed in the spider genome (Paese et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: Sox21b-1 and Sox21b-2 possibly arose from the WGD event in the ancestor of arachnopulmonates rather than by a more recent tandem duplication.
source: This suggests that Sox21b-1 and Sox21b-2 possibly arose from the WGD event in the ancestor of arachnopulmonates (Schwager et al., 2017) rather than by a more recent tandem duplication (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the genomic location and phylogenetic analysis, supported by a citation.

claim: Sox21b-1 mRNA is present in the Balbiani's body of pre-vitellogenic P. tepidariorum oocytes.
source: Pre-vitellogenic P. tepidariorum oocytes contain a Balbiani's body (Jedrzejowska and Kubrakiewicz, 2007), where maternally deposited factors are enclosed, and we found that Sox21b-1 is abundant in this region, indicating that it is maternally contributed (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Sox21b-1 is maternally contributed in P. tepidariorum.
source: Pre-vitellogenic P. tepidariorum oocytes contain a Balbiani's body (Jedrzejowska and Kubrakiewicz, 2007), where maternally deposited factors are enclosed, and we found that Sox21b-1 is abundant in this region, indicating that it is maternally contributed (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is inferred from the presence of Sox21b-1 mRNA in the Balbiani's body, which contains maternally deposited factors.

claim: Sox21b-1 mRNA is not detected after fertilization until early stage 5 in P. tepidariorum.
source: However, after fertilization we did not detect Sox21b-1 mRNA until early stage 5, when weak expression is detected throughout the germ disc, with stronger expression in more central cells (Figure 1B–C).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: At early stage 5, weak Sox21b-1 expression is detected throughout the germ disc, with stronger expression in more central cells.
source: However, after fertilization we did not detect Sox21b-1 mRNA until early stage 5, when weak expression is detected throughout the germ disc, with stronger expression in more central cells (Figure 1B–C).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: At late stage 5, Sox21b-1 expression becomes more restricted to the centre of the germ disc.
source: At late stage 5, expression becomes more restricted to the centre of the germ disc (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: In early stage 6 embryos, Sox21b-1 is observed in the middle of the presumptive prosoma in a broad stripe.
source: In early stage 6 embryos, Sox21b-1 is observed in the middle of the presumptive prosoma in a broad stripe (Figure 1E), which develops further during stage 7 in the region where the leg-bearing segments will form (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The Sox21b-1 expression pattern in early stage 6 resembles the previously described expression of the gap gene hb.
source: This expression pattern resembles the previously described expression of the gap gene hb (Schwager et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior research supported by a citation.

claim: Dynamic expression of Sox21b-1 is observed in the SAZ and the most anterior region of the germ band during stages 6-8.
source: During these and subsequent stages, dynamic expression of Sox21b-1 is observed in the SAZ and the most anterior region of the germ band that will give rise to the head segments (Figure 1H–I).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 1H-I.

claim: Later in development, the expression of Sox21b-1 resembles that of SoxNeuro (SoxN), another Group B Sox gene.
source: Later in development, the expression of Sox21b-1 resembles that of SoxNeuro (SoxN), another Group B Sox gene (Paese et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior research by the authors supported by a citation.

claim: Sox21b-1 expression is similar to that of both SoxN and Dichaete in the D. melanogaster neuroectoderm and segregating neuroblasts.
source: This expression is similar to that of both SoxN and Dichaete in the D. melanogaster neuroectoderm and segregating neuroblasts, however in spiders the neuroectoderm does not produce stem cell like neuroblasts, but instead clusters of delaminating cells that adopt the neural fate (Paese et al., 2017; Stollewerk and Chipman, 2006; McKimmie et al., 2005) (Figure 1H–I).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior research supported by citations.

claim: In spiders the neuroectoderm does not produce stem cell like neuroblasts, but instead clusters of delaminating cells that adopt the neural fate.
source: This expression is similar to that of both SoxN and Dichaete in the D. melanogaster neuroectoderm and segregating neuroblasts, however in spiders the neuroectoderm does not produce stem cell like neuroblasts, but instead clusters of delaminating cells that adopt the neural fate (Paese et al., 2017; Stollewerk and Chipman, 2006; McKimmie et al., 2005) (Figure 1H–I).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Expression of the related group B Sox genes, Dichaete and Sox21b-2 are not detected in P. tepidariorum during embryonic development.
source: Expression of the related group B Sox genes, Dichaete and Sox21b-2 are not detected in P. tepidariorum during embryonic development (Paese et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: Three phenotypic classes were observed after Sox21b-1 knockdown, which were consistent between both non-overlapping Sox21b-1 fragments used for RNAi.
source: We observed three phenotypic classes, which were consistent between both non-overlapping Sox21b-1 fragments we used for RNAi (Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Supplementaryfile 1).
evidence: This is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 2 and supplementary data.

claim: Class I Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos developed a presumptive head region, as well as normal cheliceral, pedipalpal and first leg-bearing (L1) segments.
source: Class I embryos developed a presumptive head region (Figure 2A–C), as well as normal cheliceral, pedipalpal and first leg-bearing (L1) segments (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: The identity of cheliceral, pedipalpal and L1 segments in Class I Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos was confirmed by expression of labial (lab) in the pedipalps and L1, and Deformed-A (Dfd-A) in L1.
source: The identity of these segments was confirmed by expression of labial (lab) in the pedipalps and L1, and Deformed-A (Dfd-A) in L1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–D.

claim: In Class I Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos, the leg-bearing segments L2-L4, as well as all of the opisthosomal segments were missing.
source: However, the other three leg-bearing segments, L2 - L4, as well as all of the opisthosomal segments were missing in Class I embryos.
evidence: This is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Class I Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos exhibited a truncated germ band, terminating in disorganised tissue in the region of the SAZ.
source: These embryos exhibited a truncated germ band, terminating in disorganised tissue in the region of the SAZ (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 2C.

claim: In Class II Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos, only the head region and the cheliceral and pedipalpal segments differentiated.
source: In the case of Class II phenotypes, embryos only differentiated the head region and the cheliceral and pedipalpal segments (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–B): all leg-bearing segments of the prosoma and opisthosomal segments produced from the SAZ were missing (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In Class II Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos, all leg-bearing segments of the prosoma and opisthosomal segments produced from the SAZ were missing.
source: In the case of Class II phenotypes, embryos only differentiated the head region and the cheliceral and pedipalpal segments (Figure 2D, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–B): all leg-bearing segments of the prosoma and opisthosomal segments produced from the SAZ were missing (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In Class III Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos, the germ band did not form properly from the germ disc.
source: In Class III embryos, the germ band did not form properly from the germ disc (Figure 2E)
evidence: This is supported by RNAi knockdown experiments shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The formation of the primary thickening occurs normally at stage 4 in Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos.
source: We observed that the formation of the primary thickening occurs normally at stage 4 (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003; Pechmann, 2016; Pechmann et al., 2017), but subsequently the cumulus, the group of mesenchymal cells that arise as the primary thickening at the centre of the germ disc, fails to migrate properly to the rim of the germ disc during stage 5 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by observations of Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: In Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos, the cumulus fails to migrate properly to the rim of the germ disc during stage 5.
source: We observed that the formation of the primary thickening occurs normally at stage 4 (Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2003; Pechmann, 2016; Pechmann et al., 2017), but subsequently the cumulus, the group of mesenchymal cells that arise as the primary thickening at the centre of the germ disc, fails to migrate properly to the rim of the germ disc during stage 5 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by observations of Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Migration of the cumulus is required for the transition from germ disc to germ band.
source: Since migration of the cumulus is required for the transition from germ disc to germ band, this observation at least in part explains the subsequent Class III phenotype.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that cumulus migration failure leads to Class III phenotype.

claim: At the germ disc stage, there is no detectable cell death in control embryos.
source: At the germ disc stage, there is no detectable cell death in control embryos (n = 10), but we observed some small clusters of apoptotic cells in the Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos (n = 10) (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A–B).
evidence: This is supported by Caspase-3 staining shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4A.

claim: Small clusters of apoptotic cells are observed in Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos at the germ disc stage.
source: At the germ disc stage, there is no detectable cell death in control embryos (n = 10), but we observed some small clusters of apoptotic cells in the Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos (n = 10) (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A–B).
evidence: This is supported by Caspase-3 staining shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4B.

claim: At stage 9, a few cells expressed Caspase-3 in the posterior-most part of the SAZ in control embryos.
source: At stage 9, a few cells expressed Caspase-3 in the posterior-most part of the SAZ (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C), but we did not observe cell death in this region of Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos (Figure 2—figure supplement 4D).
evidence: This is supported by Caspase-3 staining shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4C.

claim: Cell death was not observed in the SAZ region of Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos at stage 9.
source: At stage 9, a few cells expressed Caspase-3 in the posterior-most part of the SAZ (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C), but we did not observe cell death in this region of Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos (Figure 2—figure supplement 4D).
evidence: This is supported by Caspase-3 staining shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4D.

claim: Pronounced cell death was detected in the anterior extraembryonic layer of Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos at stage 9.
source: However, we did detect pronounced cell death in the anterior extraembryonic layer of the same embryos (n = 10) (Figure 2—figure supplement 4D).
evidence: This is supported by Caspase-3 staining shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4D.

claim: Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos show decreased cell proliferation compared to controls at stages 5 and 9.
source: Expression of PHH3 at stages 5 and 9 indicated that Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos show decreased cell proliferation compared to controls (n = 10 for each) (Figure 2—figure supplement 4E–H).
evidence: This is supported by PHH3 staining shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4E–H.

claim: Cells were clearly larger in Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos compared to controls.
source: Interestingly, the cells were also clearly larger in Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos compared to controls, which may reflect perturbed cell proliferation (Figure 2—figure supplement 4E–H).
evidence: This is supported by observations shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4E–H.

claim: Sox21b-1 is required for cell maintenance in several areas of the germ disc.
source: Thus, our functional analysis shows that Sox21b-1 is required for cell maintenance in several areas of the germ disc and is thus a key player in the transition from radial to axial symmetry.
evidence: This is inferred from the cell death and proliferation data.

claim: Sox21b-1 is a key player in the transition from radial to axial symmetry in spider embryos.
source: Thus, our functional analysis shows that Sox21b-1 is required for cell maintenance in several areas of the germ disc and is thus a key player in the transition from radial to axial symmetry.
evidence: This is inferred from the cumulus migration defects and cell maintenance data.

claim: In P. tepidariorum, decapentaplegic (dpp) and Ets4 are required for cumulus formation.
source: In P. tepidariorum, decapentaplegic (dpp) and Ets4 are required for cumulus formation (Pechmann et al., 2017; Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Both dpp and Ets4 were expressed normally and cumulus formation was unaffected in Sox21b-1 RNAi knockdown embryos.
source: However, both genes were expressed normally and cumulus formation was unaffected (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 3E,F.

claim: The rim of the spider germ disc develops into the head structures and is regulated in part by hh.
source: The rim of the spider germ disc develops into the head structures and is regulated in part by hh, while the mesodermal and endodermal layers of the head are specified by the mesendodermal gene forkhead (fkh) (Kanayama et al., 2011; Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The mesodermal and endodermal layers of the head are specified by the mesendodermal gene forkhead (fkh).
source: The rim of the spider germ disc develops into the head structures and is regulated in part by hh, while the mesodermal and endodermal layers of the head are specified by the mesendodermal gene forkhead (fkh) (Kanayama et al., 2011; Akiyama-Oda and Oda, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: hh is expressed at the rim of the germ disc in the ectoderm and remains unaffected by Sox21b-1 knockdown.
source: hh is expressed at the rim of the germ disc in the ectoderm (Figure 3D) (Kanayama et al., 2011) and remains unaffected by Sox21b-1 knockdown (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 3D and 3H.

claim: fkh is expressed in cells around the rim, as well as in the centre of the germ disc in mesendodermal cells.
source: fkh is also expressed in cells around the rim, as well as in the centre of the germ disc in mesendodermal cells (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos both fkh expression domains are lost.
source: In Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos both of these fkh expression domains are lost (Figure 3G), and it therefore appears that Sox21b-1 is required for specification of mesendodermal cells in the germ disc of spider embryos.
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Sox21b-1 is required for specification of mesendodermal cells in the germ disc of spider embryos.
source: In Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos both of these fkh expression domains are lost (Figure 3G), and it therefore appears that Sox21b-1 is required for specification of mesendodermal cells in the germ disc of spider embryos.
evidence: This is inferred from the loss of fkh expression in Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos.

claim: In the germ disc at stage 5, invaginating cells form a second layer.
source: Indeed, in the germ disc at stage 5, when fkh expression commences, we observed invaginating cells forming a second layer (Figure 2—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: This is supported by observations shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2G.

claim: In Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos a lower number of invaginating cells are observed, which exhibit larger nuclei compared to controls.
source: However, in Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos we observed a lower number of invaginating cells, which exhibit larger nuclei compared to controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 2H).
evidence: This is supported by observations shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2H.

claim: In both spiders and flies, the twist (twi) gene is involved in mesoderm specification.
source: In both spiders and flies, the twist (twi) gene is involved in mesoderm specification (Yamazaki et al., 2005)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: In the wild type, twi is expressed in the visceral mesoderm of the limb buds from L1 to L4, in the opisthosomal segments O1 to O4 and in an anterior mesodermal patch in the central part of the developing head.
source: In the wild type, twi is expressed in the visceral mesoderm of the limb buds from L1 to L4, in the opisthosomal segments O1 to O4 and in an anterior mesodermal patch in the central part of the developing head (Yamazaki et al., 2005) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research and gene expression data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2E.

claim: In Sox21b-1 class I embryos, the head expression of twi persists, but expression in all the limb and opisthosomal segments is lower or absent.
source: While the head expression persists in Sox21b-1 class I embryos, expression in all the limb and opisthosomal segments is lower or absent (Figure 2—figure supplement 2F).
evidence: This is supported by gene expression analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2F.

claim: In control embryos, three layers of cells can be identified in the anterior-most region of the embryo.
source: In orthogonal projections the anterior-most region of the embryo, three layers of cells can be identified in control embryos (Figure 2—figure supplement 2I).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2I.

claim: In Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos the formation of cell layers is perturbed in the anterior-most region.
source: However, in Sox21b-1 knockdown embryos the formation of these layers is perturbed (Figure 2—figure supplement 2J).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2J.

claim: Ectodermal segmentation in the prosomal region occurs even when there is a reduction in the internal layers of the embryo.
source: These data suggest that the ectodermal segmentation in the prosomal region occurs even when there is a reduction in the internal layers of the embryo.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that some segments form despite reduced mesoderm.

claim: In P. tepidariorum, formation of the SAZ and production of posterior segments requires the Wnt8 and Delta-Notch signalling pathways.
source: In P. tepidariorum, formation of the SAZ and production of posterior segments requires the Wnt8 and Delta-Notch signalling pathways (McGregor et al., 2008b; Schönauer et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Interactions between Wnt8 and Delta-Notch pathways regulate hairy (h) and, via cad, the expression of pair-rule gene orthologues including eve.
